fact: FieldTurf Landscape, a turf maker, puts its weekly care routine (walking the lawn for debris and pet messes, clearing leaves and twigs, brushing high-traffic paths and rinsing when it hasn’t rained) at 15 to 30 minutes.
quote: This 15-30 minute routine is the foundation of good turf care. … Do a quick visual inspection to spot any debris, spills, or pet messes. … Use a leaf blower or a light rake to clear away any leaves, twigs, or other organic matter. … In high-traffic areas (like paths from the patio door to the garden), use your stiff-bristled broom to brush the grass fibers up. … If it hasn’t rained recently or if pollen counts are high, give the lawn a quick rinse with the garden hose to wash away dust and allergens.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape adds a monthly session that brushes the whole lawn in one direction and then the other, checks the edges for weeds and washes the entire lawn with a hose.
quote: Once a month, spend a little more time on a more thorough cleaning. … Brush the entire lawn surface with your stiff-bristled broom or power brush. Be systematic, working in one direction and then the other to ensure all fibers are lifted. … Inspect the edges of your turf installation. Pull any weeds that may have sprouted along the perimeter. … Give the entire lawn a good washing with the hose to flush out smaller dust and dirt particles that have settled deeper into the turf.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape recommends a light rinse and debris removal weekly, a thorough brushing monthly and a deep cleaning two to four times a year, more or less often depending on use, pets and local climate.
quote: We recommend a light rinse and debris removal weekly, a more thorough brushing monthly, and a deep cleaning seasonally (2-4 times per year). The frequency can change based on usage, whether you have pets, and your local climate conditions.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape suggests a deep clean once a year, done yourself or through the annual maintenance service many installers offer, which deep cleans the surface, checks the seams and tops up the infill.
quote: Once a year, consider a professional-level deep clean. You can do this yourself with a pressure washer (following the safety rules above) and a turf-safe cleaning solution. Alternatively, many professional turf installers offer an annual maintenance service. They will use specialized sports turf maintenance equipment to deep clean the surface, check seam integrity, and top up the turf infill levels for you.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: In FieldTurf Landscape’s deep clean, a sanitizer sprayed across the whole lawn is left for 10 to 15 minutes before the lawn is rinsed.
quote: Use a turf-safe sanitizer or a homemade solution of equal parts white vinegar and water. Apply it evenly across the surface using a pump sprayer. … Allow the solution to sit for 10-15 minutes to work on any bacteria or algae.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape suggests a walk-behind power brush for larger lawns or heavy foot traffic, to lift matted fibers and spread infill faster than a hand broom.
quote: For larger lawns or those with heavy foot traffic, a mechanical power brush is a fantastic piece of artificial turf maintenance equipment. This walk-behind machine uses a rotating cylindrical brush to quickly and effectively lift matted fibers and redistribute infill.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape tells dog owners to hose down each spot after picking up solids and to apply an enzyme turf deodorizer, typically once or twice a month, especially in hot weather.
quote: After picking up solids and in areas where your pet urinates, hose the spot down thoroughly with water. This dilutes the urine and washes it through the turf’s drainage system. … For persistent odor control, especially in hot weather, regularly use an enzyme-based turf deodorizer. … Simply spray the affected areas according to the product directions, typically once or twice a month.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape advises blowing a home putting green off on a low setting daily or before each use, because even seeds or small twigs can affect a putt.
quote: Even tiny debris like seeds or small twigs can affect a putt. Use a leaf blower on a low setting daily or before each use to keep the surface immaculate.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape says weeds cannot grow through turf backing, but airborne seeds can sprout in the infill or around the edges.
quote: Weeds can’t grow through the turf’s backing, but airborne seeds can sometimes sprout in the infill layer or around the edges.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape says fall leaves left on turf over winter can decompose into a layer of organic matter that impedes drainage and encourages moss.
quote: As leaves begin to fall, it’s important to remove them regularly. If left to sit over winter, they can decompose and create a layer of organic matter that can impede drainage and encourage moss growth.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: Arithmetic on FieldTurf Landscape’s figure, not the maker’s statement: a 15 to 30 minute routine done every week of a 52-week year comes to 13 to 26 hours a year, before any monthly or seasonal work.
quote: This 15-30 minute routine is the foundation of good turf care.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance (weekly routine; hours a year are our arithmetic)
notes: 52 × 15 min = 780 min = 13 h; 52 × 30 min = 1,560 min = 26 h. Derived, not stated by the source.

fact: SYNLawn, a turf maker, lists what a professional maintenance visit covers: power brushing, odor removal and antimicrobial treatment, clearing organic debris, grooming matted areas, replenishing infill and clearing drainage blockages.
quote: Here’s what you can expect from a pro maintenance service: Deep Cleaning & Sanitization: Power brushing, odor removal, and turf-safe antimicrobial treatments. Debris & Leaf Removal: Clearing organic buildup that can block drainage. Fiber Rejuvenation: Brushing and grooming to lift matted areas. Infill Replenishment: Restoring cushioning for even and comfortable support. Drainage Optimization: Clearing blockages and optimizing water flow.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn recommends professional maintenance once or twice a year for most lawns and quarterly for pet owners, high-traffic areas and commercial properties.
quote: We recommend annual or biannual maintenance for most lawns and quarterly service for pet owners, high-traffic areas, and commercial properties.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn’s spring routine is a hose rinse to wash off the dust, pollen and dirt of the colder months and a check after a harsh winter for seams that need reinforcing and infill that needs replenishing.
quote: A garden hose is usually enough to wash away dust, pollen, and dirt that may have accumulated during colder months. … If your turf has been exposed to harsh winter weather, now is a good time to check for seams that may need reinforcement or any infill that needs replenishing.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn says warmer temperatures can intensify pet-waste odors, so pet areas need rinsing more often in summer, with enzyme cleaners.
quote: Warmer temperatures can intensify odors from pet waste. Rinse pet areas more frequently and use enzyme-based cleaners to neutralize smells.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn says barbecue, pool-chemical and sunscreen spills can leave residues on turf and should be cleaned up quickly with mild detergent and water.
quote: Barbecues, pool chemicals, and sunscreen spills can leave residues on turf. Clean up spills quickly using mild detergent and water to prevent buildup.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn warns that grills, fire pits or other heat sources set directly on turf might warp its fibers.
quote: High temperatures won’t damage artificial grass, but placing grills, fire pits, or other heat sources directly on the turf might cause fibers to warp.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn says turf in snowy areas should be in good condition before the colder months, with any drainage problem fixed before winter.
quote: If you live in an area that experiences snow, ensure that your turf is in good condition before the colder months. Any existing drainage issues should be resolved before winter sets in.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn says rock salt and chemical de-icers can degrade turf fibers and backing, and to let ice thaw naturally instead.
quote: Rock salt and chemical de-icers can degrade turf fibers and backing materials. Instead, let ice thaw naturally or use a broom to brush off any light frost.
source_label: SYNLawn, How to Maintain Your Artificial Grass

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual says a customer must be able to show they followed its installation and care guidelines to make a claim under its written coverage.
quote: Customer must demonstrably comply with “SYNLawn Installation Guidelines” and “SYNLawn Care & Maintenance guidelines,” to qualify for statutory or contractual warranty claims.
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual ties how often turf needs brushing to foot traffic, and counts multiple dogs, heavy play by children and well-used paths as high-traffic areas.
quote: The frequency for suggested brushing is directly related to the amount of foot traffic you have in your turf area. … High traffic areas might include, but are not limited to: Commercial applications Multiple dogs Heavy play activity by children Paths in the yard that are traveled more often
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual warns that landscape crews often set equipment down on turf and melt it, naming tree trimming and leaf blowing as common examples, and asks owners to discuss it with the contractor first.
quote: Landscape crews will often set equipment down on synthetic turf causing melt, please discuss ahead of time with your contractor’ Tree trimming and leaf blowing are common examples.
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual notes that utility locators have at times painted gas and water line marks on top of synthetic turf.
quote: Utilities may not recognize synthetic turf and have at times painted atop it to designate gas and water lines.
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)

fact: CSU Extension’s PlantTalk Colorado says artificial turf needs no mowing, fertilizing or watering and is sold as virtually maintenance free, but it collects leaves and wind-blown dirt and debris that must be removed, and pet waste on it is problematic.
quote: The companies that sell and install these lawns insist that they are virtually maintenance free, but artificial turf collects leaves and other wind-blown dirt and debris that must somehow be removed. Pet feces and urine deposits are problematic. … Although artificial turf does not require mowing, fertilizing, or watering and can be a legitimate solution for high traffic sites
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado 1537: Artificial Turf for Lawns

fact: CSU Extension’s PlantTalk Colorado says female cottonwoods shed their cotton in June, often so heavily that nearby lawns turn white.
quote: Cotton shed by female trees in June is often so abundant that it turns nearby lawns white.
source_label: CSU Extension, PlantTalk Colorado 1758: Cottonwood Cotton

fact: CSU Extension says a bluegrass or fescue lawn may need mowing every three to four days in spring and once every seven to 10 days when heat, drought or cold slow its growth.
quote: You may have to mow a bluegrass or fescue lawn every three to four days during the spring when it is actively growing but only once every seven to 10 days when growth is slowed by heat, drought, or cold.
source_label: CSU Extension, Lawn Care Basics

fact: At NOAA’s Fort Collins station, average monthly snowfall runs 6.7 inches in January, 7.6 in February, 9.4 in March, 6.2 in April and 1.6 in May, then 0.7 in September, 4.1 in October, 7.6 in November and 7.5 in December (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053005 FT COLLINS — MLY-SNOW-NORMAL Jan 6.7 · Feb 7.6 · Mar 9.4 · Apr 6.2 · May 1.6 · Jun 0.0 · Jul 0.0 · Aug 0.0 · Sep 0.7 · Oct 4.1 · Nov 7.6 · Dec 7.5
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station FT COLLINS (USC00053005)
notes: Fetched 2026-09-25 from the NCEI data service (JSON). MLY-SNOW-NORMAL = long-term average monthly snowfall in inches. Station-to-town assignment by proximity, as in climate.json.

fact: At NOAA’s Fort Collins station, days at or above 90°F average 0.4 in May, 5.7 in June, 13.0 in July, 8.3 in August and 2.0 in September (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053005 FT COLLINS — MLY-TMAX-AVGNDS-GRTH090 May 0.4 · Jun 5.7 · Jul 13.0 · Aug 8.3 · Sep 2.0 · Oct–Apr 0.0
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station FT COLLINS (USC00053005)
notes: MLY-TMAX-AVGNDS-GRTH090 = average number of days in the month with a high of 90°F or more.

fact: At NOAA’s Greeley UNC station, days at or above 90°F average 2.1 in May, 11.6 in June, 20.0 in July, 16.8 in August and 7.3 in September (1991–2020 normals).
quote: USC00053553 GREELEY UNC — MLY-TMAX-AVGNDS-GRTH090 Apr 0.2 · May 2.1 · Jun 11.6 · Jul 20.0 · Aug 16.8 · Sep 7.3 · Oct 0.3
source_label: NOAA NCEI U.S. Climate Normals 1991–2020, monthly, station GREELEY UNC (USC00053553)
notes: Station name confirmed with includeStationName=true on 2026-09-25. Station-to-town assignment by proximity.

fact: Of the 536 hail reports NOAA logged in Weld County from 2011 through 2025, 486 came in May through August, June was the busiest month with 161, and none came from November through March.
quote: CZ_NAME = WELD, EVENT_TYPE = Hail, 2011–2025, reports by BEGIN month: Apr 7 · May 100 · Jun 161 · Jul 128 · Aug 97 · Sep 39 · Oct 4 · Nov–Mar 0 · total 536
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files 2011–2025 (county = Weld), reports by month
notes: Counted 2026-09-25 from the 15 details files (d2011–d2025, the versions listed on the NCEI directory that day); totals match noaa-hail-weld-2011-2025. 486 = 100 + 161 + 128 + 97 (our sum). Distinct hail days by month: Apr 3, May 33, Jun 44, Jul 38, Aug 28, Sep 9, Oct 1.

fact: All 253 hail reports NOAA logged in Larimer County from 2011 through 2025 came from May through September, 198 of them in June and July.
quote: CZ_NAME = LARIMER, EVENT_TYPE = Hail, 2011–2025, reports by BEGIN month: May 20 · Jun 113 · Jul 85 · Aug 33 · Sep 2 · Oct–Apr 0 · total 253
source_label: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database, details files 2011–2025 (county = Larimer), reports by month
notes: Counted 2026-09-25 from the same 15 details files; totals match noaa-hail-larimer-2011-2025. 198 = 113 + 85 (our sum). Distinct hail days by month: May 7, Jun 25, Jul 20, Aug 14, Sep 2.

fact: Firestone’s development code requires artificial turf to be cleaned and groomed to keep its appearance, and free of weeds, holes, tears, stains, seam separations, depressions, odors and excessive wear.
quote: Artificial turf shall be maintained in a manner to mimic healthy living turf. … Artificial turf shall be cleaned as necessary and groomed to maintain its appearance. … Artificial turf areas shall not contain weeds, holes, tears, stains, discolorations, seam separations, uplifted surfaces, heat degradation, depressions, odors, excessive wear, or similar deformities and measures of deterioration.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.f (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through the Municode content API (jobId 488870, productId 18062) for the same node.

fact: FieldTurf Landscape’s basic turf toolkit is a push broom with synthetic bristles, a garden hose and a plastic or bamboo leaf rake, with a leaf blower for light debris and nothing metal.
quote: Choose a broom with synthetic bristles, not metal or wire, as metal can damage the turf fibers. … A simple hose is your primary cleaning tool. … A lightweight plastic or bamboo leaf rake is excellent for removing larger debris like fallen leaves and twigs without harming the turf blades. Avoid sharp metal rakes. … A leaf blower is an effective tool for clearing leaves, pine needles, and other light debris from your turf surface.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape allows a pressure washer on turf only with a wide-angle nozzle, at least a foot from the surface and under 1,500 PSI.
quote: Yes, but with great caution. Use a wide-angle nozzle, keep it at least one foot away from the surface, and ensure the pressure is low (under 1500 PSI).
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance

fact: FieldTurf Landscape, which sells turf, says keeping a turf system in good condition can extend its life from 10 to 15 years to 20 years or more.
quote: By keeping the components of your turf system in good condition, you can easily extend its life from 10-15 years to 20 years or more, giving you an excellent return on your investment.
source_label: FieldTurf Landscape, The Ultimate Guide to Artificial Turf Maintenance
notes: A seller’s claim; no independent measurement behind it was found. Pages present it as the maker’s statement.

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual says new turf needs a stabilization period of at least two weeks, varying with local conditions and use, during which minor adjustments to the turf and installation may be needed.
quote: SYNLawn products/systems require a minimum two (2) week stabilization period. This period of time varies depending on local conditions, use, and product/system specifications. During this time, it may be necessary to make minor adjustments to the product and installation.
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)

fact: SYNLawn’s care manual warns against water spray above 300 psi, which can severely damage turf and displace infill.
quote: Do not use high-pressure water spray with stream force in excess of 300 psi as this can severely damage the turf and displace any infill material.
source_label: SYNLawn Care and Maintenance Manual (SCM.v230517, May 17, 2023)
